defaults.evidence: Values differ by floor. GROUND FLOOR (FFL +0.90; the ceiling-level tags labelled 'ceiling line level' sit at 3.00 above FFL): every door and glazed opening in both elevations runs from the floor to 3.00. That covers D1 and D3 (frames 2.95, leaves 2.90), AD1 and AW1 (frames 2.95-3.00), AW14, the family-room and living-room glazing, and the link passage. UPPER FLOOR (FFL +4.80; ceiling 2.90): every window frame runs from the floor to 2.60 (AW12, AW14, the master-bedroom west window, the stair-hall and living-room glazing; AW17 is drawn to 2.55). Structural openings, the open screen bay and the link passage run to the 2.90 ceiling. No upper-floor door appears in either elevation. No window in either elevation has a raised sill: the lowest frame is at 0.00-0.05. Upper windows have a fixed lower pane up to 0.975 and opening sashes from 1.00 to 2.50. Double-height glazing runs unbroken from ground FFL to 6.50 (upper FFL + 2.60). Summary: door head 3.00 (ground-floor exterior doors only; interior and upper-floor doors unknown, no higher than the 2.90 upper ceiling); window sill 0.00; window head 2.60 on the upper floor and 3.00 on the ground floor; full-height glazing top 3.00 on the ground floor and 2.60 on the upper floor. The plan's project defaults (door head 2.10, window sill 0.90, window head 2.10) do not fit this house.

caveats: Coverage is limited. Both elevations are side elevations (they carry the letter grids A-M) and show the main house only. elev_left is the west face of the central volume seen from the courtyard: the west wing (x 7.7-14.8) and its facades are not drawn, and the glazed link is cut. elev_right is the east face of the main house: the east service/staff block (ground x 40-54, upper x 114-127) and its stair are not drawn. There is no north or south elevation. So most of the plan's openings get no height from this drawing: the north and south facades, the whole west wing, the staff block and every interior door. The 17 entries here cover 14 distinct openings (the stair-hall window, the link and the living-room glazing are each split into a ground and an upper entry).

Both elevations are drawn at 2:1. The level tags put 7.80 drawing units per 3.90 m storey, and opening widths match the plan at a factor of 2.000 within 3 mm. Heights are (y_elev - datum) / 2 from the TAG-LEV triangle tips: +0.90 is at y 44.7934 (left) and 43.4679 (right); +4.80 is at 52.5934 and 51.2679.

Several grid bubbles in the elevations are misplaced: A, K and M in elev_left, and M, G, C and A in elev_right (A and M sit at the building edges, A-to-M is 17.1 m instead of 19.37 m). Only D, F and H (elev_left) and J and H (elev_right) fall exactly on the plan grid lines. The mapping was fitted on those bubbles plus the jambs, so do not map anything through the other bubbles.

AD1 (east glazed bay): the elevation draws a 3.50 m sliding door (y 16.858-20.361) followed by wall, but the plan's bay glazing runs to y 20.908 (4.05 m). The elevation and plan disagree by 0.55 m, probably a design revision. I gave the plan's ends.

AW14 on the ground floor (east elevation, y 23.46-24.46): there is no matching window in the ground plan, only a single line at x 32.398 and a duct box. planA/planB are null; the candidate position is in its notes. The upper AW17 directly above matches the upper plan exactly. The tag AW14 is used twice, for this 0.95 m light and for the 2.40 m upper east window.
Stair-hall window: the elevation's glass is 1.20 m wide but the plan's is 1.305 m (the south end differs by 0.10 m).

Upper-floor windows: the frames stop at 2.60 but the structural opening (wall lines) runs to the 2.90 ceiling. The 2.60-2.90 band is not drawn as glass and is treated as solid (lintel from 2.60). The fixed lower panes (0.05-0.975) carry a glass-reflection hatch, so I read them as glass; if they are opaque, the effective sill would be 1.00.

The double-height glazing (stair hall, living-room west wall) is one curtain window from ground FFL to 6.50. It is split into a ground entry (0.00-3.90, including a glass transom in the floor zone, because there is no slab behind it) and an upper entry (0.00-2.60).

Glazed link: on the ground floor it may be a door rather than an open passage, because the plan has an arc and a 1.0 m leaf on layer 0 at the link's east end. The link's own glass side walls (glass walls, not openings) run 0.05-2.95 on the ground floor and 0.05-2.55 above FFL on the upper floor.

elev_left also shows an X on the Section layer with the Thai label 'open' at y 12.18-14.31, 0.00-3.30. That is the open covered terrace (roof soffit 3.30 above FFL), not an opening. The family-room glazing behind it is drawn on layer HATCH (background faces) and disappears if HATCH is filtered out.

The door/window tags (AW1, D1, AD1, D3, AW12, AW14 twice, AW17) appear only in elev_right, and the drawing contains no door/window schedule; elev_left has no tags, and the plan's DSYM tags are empty. All heights here are therefore measured from the elevation geometry.

The elevations do not seem fully checked against the plan: elev_left's +9.05 tag sits 0.10 m low (its geometry gives +8.95), and there are the AD1, AW14 and stair-window mismatches above. Use the heights from the elevations but the positions from the plan.
